title: Curiosity Rover Sees Mystery Cliffs on Mars
summary:
NASA's Curiosity rover has sent home a beautiful new picture of Mars. It shows strange cliffs far away that were shaped by wind.

The rover took six photos on August 11, early in the Martian morning. Scientists put them together into one wide view. The front of the picture looks bluish, and sunlight shines on the cliffs.

These cliffs are called yardangs. They stretch about 10 miles across Mount Sharp, a mountain about 3 miles tall. Curiosity has been climbing it since 2014.

The mountain's rock layers show that long ago, Mars had lakes and streams. But the yardang layer is a puzzle. It is a different color and its layers tilt in an odd way. NASA scientist Ashwin Vasavada said it might be ash from ancient volcanoes.

Curiosity should reach the cliffs in 2027. Then it can study them with its robotic arm.
why_it_matters: Exploring Mars helps us learn how planets, including Earth, can change over time.
